overall.label: Yellow
overall.headline: Oil and inflation heat up; stocks hold near highs
overall.text: Brent is near $110 after Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites. Inflation came in hot, and markets now expect a Fed hike in December. Stocks are only 1.6% off their record. Junk-bond spreads are widening, but not breaking.

powder.label: Build — steady
powder.action: Keep new contributions going to Bond Plus. Make no transfers; the S&P fund is only 1.6% below its high, far from the 10% deploy zone (~7,040).
powder.note: Cash now earns about 4.1%, only ~0.4 pts above 3.7% inflation, so dry powder is barely holding value. If Bond Plus holds longer bonds, rising yields can cut its price. Not financial advice.

outlook.text: Earnings, the Oct 28 Fed meeting, Nov 3 midterms and Gulf attacks all land this month. Expect swings inside a range, not a trend.
Strong earnings are fighting 5%+ yields and $110 oil. Expect flat to single-digit returns, with downside risk if inflation keeps rising.
Record profits should lift stocks over a year if they hold. A 10–15% pullback along the way is normal and the likely buying window.

consensus.note: Most houses are cautious on stocks near highs and like short Treasuries. Several now see value in longer bonds at 5%+ yields.

houses.change: Dropped its long-held US stock overweight to fund a move into short-term Treasuries.
houses.fitNote: Trimming US stocks for short Treasuries mirrors sending contributions to Bond Plus.

houses.change: CIO Dan Ivascyn warned the 10-yr could reach 6%; PIMCO still likes intermediate bonds for income.
houses.fitNote: Supports waiting, but a 6% 10-yr would also hurt Bond Plus if it holds longer bonds.

houses.change: Mike Wilson calls this a late-stage correction inside a bull market and says get ready to buy.
houses.fitNote: Argues the dip is a chance to add to the S&P fund, not to keep building cash.

houses.change: Sees higher rates as a sign of firmer growth and advises sticking to long-term allocations.
houses.fitNote: Suggests keeping the normal S&P fund mix rather than tilting new money to Bond Plus.

houses.change: Raised its 10–15 year US large-cap forecast to 7.5% from 6.7%.
houses.fitNote: Long-run math still favors the S&P fund over Bond Plus, but says nothing about timing.

voices.quote: We just don't know when it's going to stop.
voices.context: On the strong economy, while warning of sticky inflation, high asset prices and rising rates.
On whether the 10-yr Treasury yield could reach 6%, a 26-year high.

street.note: These views are context, not a vote. Wall Street is often wrong together, and these views never change the dry-powder call on their own.

macro.name: Oil & Middle East
macro.note: Brent near $110 as Houthis hit Saudi oil sites and Iran attacks tankers in Hormuz.

macro.name: Inflation & Fed
macro.note: CPI 3.7% (core 2.6%), both above forecast; a December hike is now ~89% priced.

macro.name: Treasury yields
macro.note: 10-yr spiked to 5.33% on CPI day, then eased to ~5.15%.

macro.name: Labor market
macro.note: +29K jobs and 4.2% unemployment in September; the Sahm rule reads 0.00.

macro.name: Credit
macro.note: Junk spreads widened to 331bp as AI-linked debt sold off; still far from 400bp stress.

macro.name: Crypto sentiment
macro.note: Bitcoin near $82K, about 35% below its peak, as risk appetite stays weak.

pullback.note: Record close was Oct 6. The deploy zone starts at a 10% pullback (≈7,040); a 20% pullback (≈6,255) is a major opportunity.

board.change: New: cash beats inflation by ~0.4 pts

changes: Brent rose about $7 to ~$110 after Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and Aramco.
September CPI hit 3.7%, above forecast; markets now price a December Fed hike.
S&P set a record 7,819 on Oct 6, then chip stocks fell 11% in one week.
Junk-bond spreads widened 37bp to 331bp as AI-linked debt sold off.

red: 10-yr breaks above 5.5% in a disorderly way
Unemployment at 4.5%+ or Sahm rule near 0.5
green: US-Iran deal reopens Hormuz; Brent below $85

swans: Wider Gulf war: Houthi-Saudi strikes plus Iran's tanker attacks shut Hormuz
AI debt unwind: Oracle, CoreWeave debt stress spreads to credit markets
Disorderly Treasury selloff pushes the 10-yr toward 6%
